records.text_en: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is a technique that makes fine-resolution images from a radar whose own resolution is limited. The radar must be moving; it sends microwave pulses, records the echoes, and computer processing combines them as if they came from a much longer antenna.
records.text_tr: Sentetik açıklıklı radar (SAR), kendi çözünürlüğü sınırlı olan bir radardan ince çözünürlüklü görüntü üreten bir tekniktir. Radarın hareket halinde olması gerekir; mikrodalga darbeleri gönderir, yankıları kaydeder ve bilgisayar işlemesi bunları çok daha uzun bir antenden gelmiş gibi birleştirir.
records.evidence: Opening paragraphs: SAR defined as fine-resolution technique needing a moving radar; microwaves; pulses and echoes focused into a synthetic aperture.

records.text_en: Yes. SAR is an active sensor that transmits its own microwave radiation and does not depend on sunlight, so it can collect data both day and night.
records.text_tr: Evet. SAR kendi mikrodalga ışınımını gönderen aktif bir algılayıcıdır ve güneş ışığına bağlı değildir; bu nedenle hem gündüz hem gece veri toplayabilir.
records.evidence: Section 'SAR characteristics': SAR is active, transmits microwaves, does not depend on sunlight, produces data day and night.

records.note: Re-attributed. The originally cited NASA 'Get to Know SAR' page does not state the night/sunlight point; the Earth Engine tutorial states it explicitly.

records.text_en: At C-band (Sentinel-1) and L-band, SAR is largely insensitive to the atmosphere. The source names one exception for C-band: very dense rain cells.
records.text_tr: C bandında (Sentinel-1) ve L bandında SAR atmosferden büyük ölçüde etkilenmez. Kaynak, C bandı için bir istisna belirtir: çok yoğun yağış hücreleri.
records.evidence: Section 'SAR characteristics', advantages list: insensitive to atmosphere in C-band (except very dense rain cells) and L-band.

The Earth Engine tutorial supports atmosphere-insensitivity for C- and L-band with a dense-rain exception; it does not use the word 'clouds', so the cloud wording and the general 'depends on band and conditions' claim were removed.

records.text_en: NISAR is a synthetic aperture radar mission run as a partnership between NASA and the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), working at L-band and S-band. It monitors changes in Earth's land, water, vegetation and ice.
records.text_tr: NISAR, NASA ile Hindistan Uzay Araştırma Örgütü (ISRO) ortaklığında yürütülen, L ve S bantlarında çalışan bir sentetik açıklıklı radar görevidir. Dünya'nın kara, su, bitki örtüsü ve buz alanlarındaki değişimleri izler.
records.evidence: Quick Facts paragraph and Mission Characteristics table: NASA-ISRO partnership; L- and S-band; monitors land, water, vegetation, ice.

records.text_en: Backscatter is the part of the transmitted radar signal that bounces back to the radar. Its strength depends mainly on the roughness and electrical properties of the surface, and is also shaped by wetness, slope, how the size of surface features compares with the wavelength, and polarization.
records.text_tr: Geri saçılım, gönderilen radar sinyalinin radara geri dönen kısmıdır. Gücü esas olarak yüzeyin pürüzlülüğüne ve elektriksel özelliklerine bağlıdır; ıslaklık, eğim, yüzey ayrıntılarının dalga boyuna göre boyutu ve polarizasyon da onu etkiler.
records.evidence: Second paragraph defines backscatter and its dependence on roughness and conductivity; 'Interpreting Radar Images' lists wetness, slopes, wavelength-sized features, polarization.

records.note: Trimmed: 'brightness alone does not prove what an object is' is not stated on the page (it only says interpretation is not straightforward).

records.text_en: Calm water and other smooth surfaces look black in SAR images because the radar pulse is reflected away from the spacecraft. Water roughened by wind can look bright when its waves are close in size to the radar wavelength.
records.text_tr: Durgun su ve diğer pürüzsüz yüzeyler SAR görüntülerinde siyah görünür, çünkü radar darbesi uzay aracından uzağa yansır. Rüzgârla pürüzlenen su ise dalgalarının boyu radar dalga boyuna yakın olduğunda parlak görünebilir.
records.evidence: 'Interpreting Radar Images' rules of thumb: calm water appears black, pulse reflects away; wind-roughened water can backscatter brightly.

records.text_en: Each pixel of a SAR image has an amplitude and a phase. After calibration the amplitude is proportional to how reflective the surface is, while the phase depends on the distance the wave travelled, delays in the atmosphere and a contribution from the reflecting surface.
records.text_tr: Bir SAR görüntüsünün her pikselinin bir genliği ve bir fazı vardır. Kalibrasyondan sonra genlik yüzeyin yansıtıcılığıyla orantılıdır; faz ise dalganın kat ettiği mesafeye, atmosferdeki gecikmelere ve yansıtan yüzeyin katkısına bağlıdır.
records.evidence: Paragraph on the complex image: pixel has amplitude and phase; amplitude proportional to reflectance, phase to distance, atmospheric delay, surface contribution.

records.note: Re-attributed and trimmed. Original ARSET PDF could not be fetched; the NASA SAR page supports the amplitude/phase description. The sentence that phase relations underpin InSAR deformation analysis was removed because no fetched source states it.

records.text_en: Speckle is noise caused by the coherent nature of SAR radiation; it gives even uniform areas such as a large crop field a salt-and-pepper look. It can be reduced in several ways but is hard to remove completely.
records.text_tr: Speckle (benek gürültüsü), SAR ışınımının koherent yapısından kaynaklanan gürültüdür; büyük bir tarla gibi tekdüze alanlara bile tuz-biber görünümü verir. Çeşitli yollarla azaltılabilir, ancak tamamen gidermek zordur.
records.evidence: Section 'SAR characteristics', drawbacks list: coherent radiation causes speckle, salt-and-pepper appearance, reducible but difficult to eliminate.

records.text_en: The combination of polarizations used for the transmitted and the received signal has a large effect on backscatter. Choosing the right polarization can help bring out particular topographic features.
records.text_tr: Gönderilen ve alınan sinyal için kullanılan polarizasyon birleşimi geri saçılımı büyük ölçüde etkiler. Doğru polarizasyon seçimi belirli topoğrafik özelliklerin öne çıkmasına yardımcı olabilir.
records.evidence: 'Interpreting Radar Images': transmit/receive polarization combinations strongly affect backscatter; right choice emphasizes topographic features.

The NASA SAR page supports only the general effect of transmit/receive polarization; the definition as field orientation and the VV/VH/HH/HV scattering interpretation are not in any fetched source (the Earth Engine tutorial only says Sentinel-1 IW mode is acquired in VV and VH).

records.text_en: SAR backscatter depends on the incidence angle, so the same target looks different in the near range (lower angle) and the far range (higher angle) of a swath. How strongly it changes depends on the target: flat dry soil drops off more with angle than forest does.
records.text_tr: SAR geri saçılımı geliş açısına bağlıdır; bu yüzden aynı hedef şeridin yakın menzilinde (düşük açı) ve uzak menzilinde (yüksek açı) farklı görünür. Değişimin gücü hedefe bağlıdır: düz ve kuru toprakta açıyla düşüş ormana göre daha belirgindir.
records.evidence: Section 'SAR characteristics', drawbacks: backscatter depends on incidence angle; near vs far range; dry soil drops off more than forest.
questions_en: What is the incidence angle in SAR?

records.note: Trimmed: the page does not link incidence angle to 'geometric distortions' in those words, and does not say images at different angles 'must not be compared directly' (it says such effects need to be controlled for).

records.text_en: Layover is a geometric distortion on slopes in which signals from the tops of mountains or other tall objects fall on top of other signals, so the tops appear to lean toward the sensor. Steeper slopes make it more extreme, and it shows up as bright pixels.
records.text_tr: Layover (üst üste binme), eğimli alanlarda görülen bir geometrik bozulmadır: dağların veya yüksek nesnelerin tepelerinden gelen sinyaller başka sinyallerin üzerine biner ve tepeler algılayıcıya doğru yatmış görünür. Eğim dikleştikçe etki artar ve görüntüde parlak pikseller olarak belirir.
records.evidence: 'Interpreting Radar Images': slopes cause distortion; steeper angles give more layover; mountaintops tip toward sensor; layover shows bright pixels.

records.text_en: No. According to the USGS, no scientist has ever predicted a major earthquake, and it does not expect this to become possible in the foreseeable future; a real prediction would have to give the date and time, the location and the magnitude. What scientists can do is calculate the probability that a significant earthquake will occur in a given area within a certain number of years.
records.text_tr: Hayır. USGS'e göre hiçbir bilim insanı bugüne kadar büyük bir depremi önceden tahmin edememiştir ve bunun öngörülebilir gelecekte mümkün olması beklenmemektedir; gerçek bir tahminin tarih ve saati, yeri ve büyüklüğü belirtmesi gerekir. Bilim insanlarının yapabildiği, belirli bir bölgede belirli bir yıl aralığında önemli bir deprem olma olasılığını hesaplamaktır.
records.evidence: FAQ answer, opening: nobody has predicted a major earthquake; only probabilities can be calculated; prediction must define date/time, location, magnitude.

records.text_en: NISAR monitors changes in Earth's ice. It observes land and ice-covered regions worldwide every 12 days on both ascending and descending passes, which gives a sample about every 6 days on average.

records.evidence: Quick Facts paragraph: monitors changes in ice; global observations of land and ice-covered regions every 12 days, about 6-day average revisit.

records.text_en: Buildings, bridges and other human-made objects tend to act like corner reflectors and show up as bright spots in SAR images. Buildings aligned exactly perpendicular to the flight direction give very bright returns.

records.evidence: 'Interpreting Radar Images': perpendicular-aligned buildings show very bright returns; human-made objects behave as corner reflectors, bright spots.

records.text_en: Sentinel-1 backscatter over farmland is influenced by environmental factors such as weather, land preparation and crop growth, as well as by viewing geometry and speckle. These sensor and environmental effects have to be controlled for before the observations can be interpreted.

Gözlemlerin yorumlanabilmesi için bu algılayıcı ve çevre etkilerinin kontrol altına alınması gerekir.
records.evidence: Final paragraph of 'Sentinel-1 orbits, modes, swaths, and scenes': weather, land preparation, crop growth influence backscatter; parameters must be controlled.

records.text_en: Backscatter from the same place varies between acquisitions because of sensor effects such as orbit look direction, incidence angle and speckle, as well as real environmental change, so the sensor effects have to be controlled for before changes are interpreted. Sentinel-1 scenes with the same relative orbit number are 12 days apart and have almost the same viewing configuration.
records.text_tr: Aynı yerden gelen geri saçılım, gerçek çevresel değişimin yanı sıra yörünge bakış yönü, geliş açısı ve speckle gibi algılayıcı etkileri nedeniyle de çekimden çekime değişir; bu yüzden değişimler yorumlanmadan önce algılayıcı etkilerinin kontrol altına alınması gerekir. Aynı göreli yörünge numarasına sahip Sentinel-1 sahneleri 12 gün arayla alınır ve neredeyse aynı bakış geometrisine sahiptir.
records.evidence: Section 'Sentinel-1 orbits, modes, swaths, and scenes': same relative orbit gives almost same view configuration; last paragraph: must control sensor and environmental parameters.

records.text_en: In Earth Engine's COPERNICUS/S1_GRD collection, Sentinel-1 backscatter values are expressed in decibels (dB), that is, on a logarithmic scale. The COPERNICUS/S1_GRD_FLOAT collection holds the same data without the log scaling.

records.evidence: Section 'Sentinel-1': S1_GRD is the log-scaled equivalent of S1_GRD_FLOAT; final paragraph: S1_GRD values are in decibels, logarithmic scale.

records.text_en: Interpreting SAR images is not straightforward, partly because of the non-intuitive side-looking geometry. Slopes cause geometric distortions, and brightness changes with surface roughness, wetness, wavelength and polarization.
records.text_tr: SAR görüntülerini yorumlamak kolay değildir; bunun bir nedeni sezgisel olmayan yandan bakış geometrisidir. Eğimler geometrik bozulmalara yol açar ve parlaklık yüzey pürüzlülüğüne, ıslaklığa, dalga boyuna ve polarizasyona göre değişir.
records.evidence: 'Interpreting Radar Images' intro and rules of thumb: interpretation not straightforward, side-looking geometry; slopes distort; roughness, wetness, wavelength, polarization matter.

records.source_title: What's the difference between climate and weather?
records.text_en: Weather is the state of the atmosphere at a particular place over the short term. Climate is the average of the weather patterns in a place over a longer period, usually 30 years or more.
records.text_tr: Hava durumu, belirli bir yerde atmosferin kısa süreli halidir. İklim ise bir yerdeki hava olaylarının daha uzun bir dönemdeki, genellikle 30 yıl veya daha uzun süredeki ortalamasıdır.
records.evidence: Opening definition paragraph: weather is short-term atmospheric state at a location; climate is average weather over usually 30 years or more.

records.source_title: What is the difference between earthquake early warning, earthquake forecasts, earthquake probabilities, and earthquake prediction?
records.text_en: An earthquake prediction would state when, where and how large an earthquake will be, which is not yet possible. Early warning is different: it is a notification issued after an earthquake has started, alerting people seconds to tens of seconds before the shaking waves are expected to reach them.
records.text_tr: Deprem tahmini, bir depremin ne zaman, nerede ve ne büyüklükte olacağını önceden bildirmek demektir; bu henüz mümkün değildir. Erken uyarı ise farklıdır: deprem başladıktan sonra verilen bir bildirimdir ve sarsıntı dalgalarının bulunulan yere ulaşması beklenmeden saniyeler ile onlarca saniye önce insanları uyarır.
records.evidence: FAQ summary and 'early warning' paragraph: warning issued after the quake starts, seconds to tens of seconds; prediction of when/where/size not yet possible.
